target_customer: Music fans on iPhones, with musicians as content partners
problem: Music videos and concerts on phones are flat; artists lacked an easy way to bring immersive experiences to fans' living rooms.
business_model: Free consumer app with exclusive artist AR content, no revenue model found

founders.name: Hammad Bashir
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; no bio found.

founders.name: Sonia Sharma
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; no bio found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Built AR tracks with 3D modeling, Unity and Apple ARKit, which only shipped in 2017; standard but novel tooling for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Content was exclusive per track but the approach was easy to replicate with ARKit and Snapchat style lenses.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying documented in sources; Ubiquity6 acqui-hired the team in January 2019 and stopped the Wavy app.

market_need_then: ARKit launched for iOS in 2017 creating a new capability for phone AR; no sources show measured demand for AR music.

branding.domain_note: Used downloadwavy.com, a download-prefix domain; the site returned HTTP 503 on fetch.

brand_strength.rationale: Small niche app with a handful of articles; other products share the Wavy name.

outcome_analysis: Wavy launched an iOS AR music app in mid 2018 with two experiences and was acquired by AR cloud startup Ubiquity6 in January 2019, which said the team would join and the Wavy app would not continue. No funding or traction figures are public, so the story is of an early product absorbed for its AR team rather than a standalone business.
notes: No funding round found; CB Insights lists Ubiquity6 as only investor (aggregator). CB Insights gives founding 2018 versus TechCrunch saying founded the prior year. The company site could not be fetched (503). Competitor search found only items dated 2018 or later, so the list is empty. Timing of market_timing_early is a judgment from the source that the app was discontinued, not stated by sources.
